changes of stimulation frequency alter the Ca2+ and Na+ loads of cardiac myocytes in a manner that is consistent with the force-frequency relationship.
changes in intracellular [Ca] and [Na] and sarcoplasmatic reticulum Ca content underlie the positive force-frequency relationship in rat ventricular cells.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the cellular and molecular bases of the force-frequency relationship in the heart.
how the heart responds to changes in the rate of electrical stimulation, i.e. how heart rate influences the contractile performance of cardiac muscle cells.
the regulation of cardiac contraction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in rat ventricular cells, the force-frequency relationship is a reflection of the balance between the sarcoplasmatic reticulum Ca load and the Na-Ca exchange current.
a positive force frequency relationship is associated with a greater change of [Na+] with changes of frequency and with a larger Ca2+ load in the sarcoplasmatic reticulum.
the force-frequency relation is a function of the frequency of stimulation, which is the primary determinant of the force-frequency relation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a positive force-frequency relation in rat ventricular cells is associated with a positive inotropic effect of Na+-Ca2+ exchange, and that a negative force-frequency relation is associated with an inhibitory effect of Na+- Ca2+ exchange.

in cells showing a negative force-frequency relation, the increase of Nai with increasing frequency of stimulation causes an increase in the Ca2+/Na+ exchange rate, which causes an increase in SR Ca2+ content and a decrease in Cai.
a positive force frequency response is associated with a greater ability of the cell to increase the intracellular Ca2+ load and the Ca2+ transient with an increase in stimulation frequency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the force-frequency relationship in the rat ventricle is not a single phenomenon but a spectrum of phenomena, and that the spectrum of phenomena can be understood in terms of the changes in [Na+] and [Ca2+] that occur as stimulation frequency is increased.
the force-frequency relationship of the ventricle is not a function of changes in the Ca2+-handling apparatus of the myocytes.
changes in [Na+] are a major determinant of the force-frequency relationship.
